title: Duskwood
body: Duskwood was once called Brightwood, a green and peaceful stretch of forest south of Stormwind, until a foul magic seeped into the land and the woods fell under a night that never fully lifts. The dead do not rest here, worgen have appeared as if from thin air to overrun the groves, and Dark Riders out of Deadwind Pass have slaughtered a farmer's family. When Stormwind recalled its guards, the people of Darkshire raised the Night Watch to defend themselves, and they have not forgiven the capital.

title: Raven Hill
body: Raven Hill was once a town of western Duskwood, long abandoned, its houses given over to the Unseen, shadowy things that drift through the ruins. A goblin trader has found shelter among the empty buildings, and the graveyard that gives the town its grim fame lies just to the north. Calor of Darkshire swears the place is haunted: shadows moving two nights running, and a light in one of the windows.

parts.body: The haunting is no monster. The shadows and the light belong to Jitters, a starving, terrified fugitive who hides among the empty houses, sure that whatever hunts him is everywhere.

title: Raven Hill Cemetery
body: North of the abandoned town sprawls the Raven Hill Cemetery, which by the end of the wars had grown to cover much of the area. It holds the graves of many who met tragic ends, and few of them lie still: skeletons walk among the headstones, ghouls claw at the earth and plague spreaders infest the eastern mausoleum. One stone bears only the name Eliza and a prayer that the earth might satisfy her hunger.

title: Twilight Grove
body: At the heart of Duskwood stands the Twilight Grove, where a great tree rises over a moonwell and a gazebo of night elf design, strange sights so far from Kalimdor. It holds one of four gateways to the Emerald Dream, the realm watched over by the green dragonflight, each beneath a great tree; the others lie in the Hinterlands, Ashenvale and Feralas.

parts.body: Yet the grove is no refuge. Dragons of Ysera's flight, corrupted and driven mad by nightmare, have come out to guard the portal and spread their madness.

title: Darkshire
body: Darkshire, once called Grand Hamlet, took its grim name when darkness fell on the forest. It is the heart of human Duskwood and the home of the Night Watch. Lord Ello Ebonlocke governs from the town hall with a council that complains endlessly of Stormwind's neglect, Madame Eva reads the cards beside the square, and the Carevin family, hunters of demons and the undead, wage their own war on the evil in the woods.

parts.body: Help has come from much farther away as well: draenei, whose people have joined the Alliance, arrive to aid a town beset on all sides by the creatures of the night.

title: Manor Mistmantle
body: Just north of Darkshire stands Manor Mistmantle, home of the recluse Stalvan Mistmantle. The grounds have gone to rot, fetid corpses shamble along the overgrown paths, and only one living thing seems to thrive there, a single flower in the garden called the Tear of Tilloa. Its master is no welcoming host. He meets intruders with threats to spill their blood, and sometimes, peering at them, takes them for someone named Tilloa.

title: Beggar's Haunt
body: In the northeast of Duskwood, near the road into Deadwind Pass, stands Beggar's Haunt, an abandoned scout tower of the Stormwind Guard. Its new tenants are Forsaken: a deathstalker and an apothecary of the Royal Apothecary Society, part of an expeditionary force sent at Varimathras's command to survey the southern lands, who would much rather nobody knew they were here.

title: Sven Yorgen
body: Sven Yorgen farmed land in western Duskwood until the day he went to Darkshire and came home to find his wife and children murdered by Dark Riders from Deadwind Pass. He rode after the killers in vain. Now he keeps a small camp on the Hushed Bank with his companion Lars, living off the land and welcoming anyone who will join his fight.

parts.body: Behind a stump by his barn lay a small book, buried in haste. Its writer had watched the slaughter of Sven's family, and Sven means to find him.
The book belonged to Jitters, the fugitive hiding in Raven Hill, who had witnessed the killing and has fled from one hiding place to the next ever since.
His completed journal tells what the riders wanted. They demanded the Scythe of Elune of Sven's wife, and when a power working through a rider's gem found her lie, the family was killed.
Morbent Fel is defeated. The Dark Riders are still at large, but a small piece of Sven's revenge has come to pass, and he promised the deed would live forever in Duskwood's legends.

title: Abercrombie
body: Abercrombie is a frail old man who lives alone in a shack beside the Raven Hill Cemetery. He once came to Darkshire often but has not been seen there in a long while; the roads are dangerous, he says, and he is not getting any younger. He seems harmless enough, asking travelers for thread, liquor, ghoul ribs and a crate the ogres stole. Yet he laughs a little too hard when they succeed, and more than once his tongue slips.

parts.body: His note to Lord Ebonlocke, once translated, gave him away: a gloating confession signed the Embalmer, who had tricked his helpers into building a fiend of flesh, bone and twisted metal to slaughter the town.
The abomination, Stitches, marched on Darkshire along the road, overran the Night Watch camp on the way, and was cut down in the center of town by its gathered defenders.

The Embalmer is a name from Darkshire's children's stories, and the story is true: a kindly alchemist, mad with grief, placed his own heart in his dead wife Eliza to revive her. It cursed her with a hunger for human flesh, and he had to keep her buried.
His heart was dug from Eliza's grave still beating, and with it his power was broken. Its magic now stands as a powerful aegis over the town he meant to see slaughtered.

title: Stalvan Mistmantle
body: Stalvan Mistmantle of Silverpine was a scholar who came south to tutor the farm children of Moonbrook, and later the children of the noble Flintridge family in Stormwind. He fell for their elder daughter, Tilloa, and when she chose another his longing turned to blood. Visiting nobles were slaughtered at the Flintridge estate, and the crime went unsolved for years, until his journal pages were matched to his signature in Darkshire's registry.

parts.body: He died in his own manor north of Darkshire. His family ring went to Madame Eva, whose premonition began the hunt, and she felt a wave of hope ripple through the tainted forest.

title: Morbent Fel
body: Morbent Fel is the necromancer behind the restless dead of Duskwood. From his house atop the Forlorn Rowe he looks down on the Raven Hill Cemetery, and the dead that fill it answer to his will. He has living accomplices too: Dextren Ward was caught selling him bodies from the cemetery and condemned to death by Lord Ebonlocke. Beside his house lies a weathered grave marked Morgan Ladimore, its dirt recently disturbed.

parts.body: Fel keeps company with the Dark Riders of Deadwind Pass: Sven Yorgen has seen the riders who killed his family speaking with him at the Forlorn Rowe.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Morbent_Fel (pre-Cataclysm: ruled the undead of Duskwood, magical barrier, Morbent's Bane)

parts.body: Bishop Farthing of Stormwind judged him immensely powerful, protected by dark enchantments that only a weapon made proof against them can break.

title: Mor'Ladim
body: Mor'Ladim is the name taken by an undead knight who wanders Duskwood, following a strange, meandering path through the Raven Hill Cemetery and the woods around it. He kills without reason, watchmen on patrol and travelers alike, and some of the Night Watch's strongest watchers have been lost to him. Commander Ebonlocke wants him laid to rest but has no one to spare for the task.

parts.body: He was once Morgan Ladimore, a knight of Duskwood who fought beside Uther in the wars of Lordaeron. He came home to find his wife beneath a gravestone, cut down three attendants in his grief and took his own life. Buried without ceremony, he rose days later.
Mor'Ladim has been struck down among the graves he haunts, and the Night Watch's patrols have one less terror to face.
Morgan believed all his family dead, but his daughter Sarah lived, and now serves as a Watcher, troubled always by the way her father died.
Sarah's ring, laid on his grave, told him she was well and that none of them held him to blame. His spirit found peace, gave up his sword Archeus, and spoke his wife's name as it was put to rest.

sources: quest 227 reward text (attacking watchmen on patrol and killing people)
